🎙
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at a meeting with Member of the Politburo and Secretary of the Central Committee of the Workers’ Party of Korea Jo Yong-won
(Moscow, November 16, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
Comrade Secretary, dear friends, I am very pleased to see you!
First of all, I would like to convey
my very best wishes
to President of the State Affairs of the DPRK
Comrade Kim Jong-un
. I greatly value
the businesslike and friendly relationship
we have developed, which undoubtedly helps us address issues and advance relations between our countries.
Your delegation has come to Moscow to take part in
the Forum of Supporters of the Struggle Against Modern Practices of Neocolonialism “For the Freedom of Nations”
.
You have a busy programme in Moscow
, including meetings with the leadership of
the United Russia party
,
Chairman of the State Duma
and, tomorrow,
Speaker of the Federation Council
. I wish you every success in your work.
🇷🇺
🇰🇵
For many decades, our countries have been bound by strong friendship, good-neighbourly relations and brotherhood in arms.
The Treaty on Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
is in force.
Last year, we marked
several anniversaries
:
Victory in the Great Patriotic War
,
the liberation of Korea
,
victory over militarist Japan
and
the end of World War II
, as well as the founding of the Workers’ Party of Korea.
⚔️
The participation of Korean People’s Army units
in
the liberation of the Kursk Region
has opened a new chapter in our countries’ brotherhood in arms.
We will never forget the heroism of the Korean soldiers
who fought shoulder to shoulder with Russian servicemen.
By the end of this year,
we plan to unveil a sculptural monument in Kursk
honouring the shared feat of the soldiers of Russia and the DPRK.
In addition, Korean military engineers and construction units have made
an important contribution
to restoring infrastructure and bringing peaceful life back to the Kursk Region.
We greatly appreciate this.
🤝
Once again, please convey
my very best wishes and
friendly greetings
to President of the State Affairs
Comrade Kim Jong-un
.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33385

🎙
Interview
with Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov by Director General of
TASS
Andrey Kondrashov
(Moscow, November 16, 2026)
Key points
:
• When I met President of Finland
Alexander Stubb
in New York during
the UN General Assembly Session
, he said something had to be done:
“We are heading down the wrong path, and this will take us somewhere we do not want to go. It will not end well”
.
I replied
:
“Listen, if that is how you feel,
take some meaningful action
. Do not just say that Ukraine will die for us, and that this is how we will defend our values”
.
• At the same
#UNGA81 Session
, I
asked
German Foreign Minister
Johann Wadephul
a very simple question. They had found
a drone at Leipzig Airport
carrying an explosive charge that had failed to detonate.
Nobody proved it was a Russian drone.
In just three days, they simply declared that the Russians were responsible and that
Russian diplomats and the Russian cultural centre would be expelled
. Against that backdrop,
I asked whether
their investigation into Nord Stream
was taking rather too long
. Johann Wadephul replied that
these were different issues
🤷‍♂️
.
•
Understandings on Ukraine that could be put down on paper
were reached in Anchorage
.
They were not simply announced on the spur of the moment. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff
visited a week before the Anchorage Summit
in August 2025 and was received by President
Vladimir Putin
. We saw that some elements of the proposal he brought involved
compromises
. But since any lasting agreement rests, to some extent, on compromise,
we accepted the American proposal
.
• Then
various interpretations
emerged: supposedly, there had been no deal, no agreement, only an initiative.
But if you propose something and I accept it, in Russia that means we have reached an agreement.
•
Europe has had numerous opportunities to act as a mediator
, starting in February 2014, when
France, Germany
and
Poland
acted as guarantors of the agreements between Ukraine’s then President
Viktor Yanukovich
and the opposition. Incidentally, Poland’s guarantor was its current Foreign Minister
Radoslaw Sikorski
, who also attended
the international forum in Abu Dhabi
where I went to speak. I recalled this there and said:
“Here is one of the guarantors”
. The morning after that agreement,
a coup took place
.
•
Dialogue on removing irritants in
#RussiaUS
relations is making slow progress
, even though I raise the issue every time I meet US Secretary of State
Marco Rubio
. We met
in New York
during the high-level week of the 81st UN General Assembly Session, and later
in Atlanta
at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
Both Sides have an interest in resolving these issues.
•
There is no reason to hail Washington’s lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel supplies as some bold move.
The Americans proudly announced that Venezuelan oil was now under their control, rather than China’s or Russia’s. We did not control anything there, nor did the Chinese: we were partners.
We are being pushed out of every energy market.
A doctrine of dominance over global energy markets has been approved and is now being put into practice.
•
We need to take a sober view of things. We must talk to the Americans.
But trying to do so while positively gushing with enthusiasm does not serve our interests. The Americans do not respect such behaviour.
• The world is not getting any simpler. Remember, we have two allies:
our Army and Navy
. Now we also have our
Aerospace and Nuclear forces
.

item.title: 🇷🇺 #Announcement At the invitation of President of the People’s Republic of China Xi Jinping
item.description: #Announcement 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 At the invitation of President of the People’s Republic of China Xi Jinping , President of the Russian Federation Vladimir Putin will pay a working visit to China on November 18-19 and attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit ( #APEC ) in Shenzhen. On November 18, Vladimir Putin will address the APEC CEO Summit , and on November 19, he will take part in the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting , where he will outline Russia’s priorities for trade and economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region. Full-scale #RussiaChina talks will take place , during which Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will discuss prospects for further strengthening relations of comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation, as well as international and regional issues. 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 🇺🇸 A trilateral meeting between Vladimir Putin and the Leaders of China and the US is planned. A separate meeting between Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump is also envisaged. In addition, the Russian President will hold bilateral meetings with the Leaders of several other countries. During his stay in Shenzhen, Vladimir Putin will also visit Shenzhen MSU-BIT University , jointly established by Lomonosov Moscow State University and Beijing Institute of Technology , and address students and faculty .

#Announcement
📆
On November 17, Manila (the Philippines)
will host
the 21st East Asia Summit (
#EAS
). The Russian delegation will be headed by Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov
.
Established in 2005,
the EAS serves
as a forum for dialogue among leaders of Asia-Pacific countries
on a broad range of political and economic issues of common interest, as well as ways to advance practical cooperation across various fields.
Since its inception,
the East Asia Summit
has identified
six priority areas of cooperation:
• Energy
• Finance
• Emergency response
• Healthcare
• Education
• Regional connectivity
☝️
However, substantive work has been carried out in only some of these areas.
***
🌐
The EAS
brings together the members
of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations
(
#ASEAN
) – Brunei, Vietnam, Indonesia, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and the Philippines – and
ASEAN’s dialogue partners
: Russia (since 2010), Australia, India, China, the Republic of Korea, New Zealand, the United States and Japan.
The ASEAN Chair also chairs the East Asia Summit
: the Philippines in 2026 and Singapore in 2027.
👉
The agenda of the 21st EAS will focus on
current issues in regional development
and
prospects for expanding practical cooperation
.
Russia advocates
broadening the EAS’s tools for practical cooperation,
with an emphasis on implementing Leaders’ decisions.
Our initiatives include
coordinating region-wide efforts to combat pandemics
, with the possibility of establishing a collective response mechanism for epidemic threats, and
setting up a standing consultation channel on tourism
. These proposals are reflected in relevant Leaders’ documents.
At
the 14th EAS Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
(Vientiane, July 27, 2024),
Russia proposed establishing cooperation on the development of remote areas.
Our country has extensive experience in this field, both in implementing national projects and in multilateral cooperation, including within the
#SCO
and
#APEC
.
Russia supports building a lasting network of links among Eurasian platforms
by bringing together the development potential of key regional mechanisms – the
#SCO
,
#ASEAN
and the
#EAEU
– which share a common commitment to constructive cooperation.
Mutual interest in establishing contacts between
#ASEAN
countries and
#BRICS
is growing
. Inviting Brazil’s leadership to ASEAN summits is becoming
a welcome tradition
: as last year, President of Brazil
Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
will attend the ASEAN Leaders’ meeting as a guest of the Chair.
🤝
The BRICS presence within the EAS continues to grow
, encompassing Russia, India, China, Indonesia, which joined BRICS in January 2025, and Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand, which have gained partner-country status.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/33369

⚡️
On November 16,
the Russian Union of Journalists
has issued
an open letter
to UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany regarding the publication of the report on the safety of journalists for 2024-2025.
The letter cites
specific cases of Russian media workers killed
whose deaths are absent from the organisation’s official statistics
, and raises questions about
the reliability and transparency of its methodology.
The Union demands
an explanation for the omission of these journalists from the report
and proposes revising the recording system to ensure uniform verification criteria and a right to appeal decisions.
✉️
FULL LETTER IN ENGLISH
|
Telegraph
***
✍️
We are writing to you on behalf of
the Russian Union of Journalists
(
#RUJ
), a professional association that regards the protection of journalists as a universal obligation, irrespective of nationality, editorial position, or political context.
Our appeal concerns
the procedures used to verify information submitted to UNESCO
regarding
the deaths of journalists and media workers
, as well as the criteria governing decisions on whether such cases are included in or excluded from official statistics.
We
do not question
the need for independent verification,
nor do we propose replacing it with official statements
issued by governments. However, we consider it essential that the verification process be
transparent
, based on
uniform and objective criteria
, provide
reasoned explanations
for decisions, and
allow for their reconsideration
on substantiated grounds.
The UNESCO Director-General’s Report for 2024–2025
(
CI-26/COUNCIL.35/6
) records
189 verified cases
of journalists and media workers killed, of which
127 occurred in countries affected by armed conflict
.
According to
the document
,
the overall impunity rate for monitored cases reached 86%
. This is important and necessary work undertaken by UNESCO:
the world needs verifiable statistics on crimes against the press
.
☝️
However, the figure of 189
does not automatically represent
an exhaustive count of all media workers who lost their lives worldwide during those two years. Rather, it represents
the number of cases that passed UNESCO’s established verification procedure
and were included in its reporting.
This distinction is fundamental.
The public has a right to know not only how many cases have been included in official statistics, but also
how many credible reports remain under verification
,
why certain cases have not been included
, and
how those decisions may be reconsidered
.
In Annex E to
the report
, UNESCO explains that information may be received from Member States, regional offices, and specialized monitoring organizations, after which the Secretariat verifies it against multiple sources.
Cases that do not meet the verification criteria continue to be monitored in accordance with internal procedures
. Meanwhile,
the public Observatory of Killed Journalists
covers cases in which the Director-General has called for an investigation or expressed condolences.
👉
This is where a systemic problem arises:
public statistics are based on decisions made by UNESCO’s leadership, yet
the public has no access to a comparably transparent procedure
explaining exclusions, the status of pending cases, or the possibility of seeking reconsideration. When decisions are made without publicly stated reasons, the absence of a name
can easily be mistaken for the absence of the death itself
.
This gives rise to four questions that cannot be left unanswered
:
•
Nikita Goldin
:
One news crew, different outcomes in official records
•
Alexander Martemyanov
:
Why did the public statement by the IFJ and EFJ not lead to action?
•
Semyon Eryomin
:
His death was also reported by Reuters
•
Yulia Kuznetsova
:
A regional editor is also a journalist
❗️
We respectfully submit for your consideration five proposals from the Russian Union of Journalists, which we strongly urge you to take into account
.
